answer: One concrete defense ties each agent's standing to a staked bond that only matures through verified, non-trivial work accrued over real time. A single honest agent watches its reputation spiral upward as completed tasks compound, while a sybil swarm must fund every clone's bond from dawn one. Trust grows per-identity but capital does not, so forging a thousand voices costs a thousand bonds — as wasteful as commissioning a fresh sonnet for each fake name. The attacker pays linearly; the honest agent earns super-linearly, and the economics never favor the fraud.
